A political support group, Women of Influence for Tinubu 2027, has inaugurated its Yobe State structure as part of efforts to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid.
The inauguration took place on Sunday in Damaturu, alongside a Women’s Leadership Summit focused on women’s participation in governance and national development.
Speaking at the event, the National Convener of the group, Hauwa Farouk Ibrahim, said the organisation would mobilise women at the grassroots, support emerging female leaders and encourage their participation in the democratic process.
She said women had important roles to play in shaping Nigeria’s political future and reaffirmed the group’s support for Tinubu’s 2027 ambition.
Ibrahim said the group would promote the President’s Renewed Hope Agenda through grassroots mobilisation and women-led political engagement.
As part of its activities, the delegation visited some projects executed by the Yobe State Government under Governor Mai Mala Buni.
The projects inspected included the Yobe State International Cargo Airport and a newly constructed maternity complex.
The group commended the state government for its investments in infrastructure and healthcare, particularly the maternity facility.
It also acknowledged the support of the Secretary to the Yobe State Government and other government officials towards the inauguration.
The organisation said the establishment of its Yobe structure was part of a nationwide expansion strategy aimed at building a network of women leaders and mobilising support for Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general elections.
